boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Marais des Cygnes (Trading Post) record (October 25, 1864) in Price's Missouri Expedition [September-October 1864]. The night approach of October 24 is context; Mine Creek (KS003) and the Marmiton (MO028) the same day are separate records, and the intervening action on the Little Osage is context, not added to any record. Campaign-wide marches, recruiting, destruction, returns and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads Provisional cavalry division and cavalry division; the live field reads zero. NPS says the Federals were outnumbered. Britton says Sanborn's brigade led, with Gravely's Sixth and Eighth Missouri State Militia and the Fourth Iowa taking the mounds, then Mitchell's and McMahan's militia, Phelps's Second Arkansas and three companies of the Second Colorado forcing the ford, with Philips's and Benteen's brigades coming up. Price says Fagan's and Marmaduke's divisions formed his rear guard.
claims.rationale: Unit identifications and a qualitative statement; no count for either side. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

open_questions: Pleasonton's (No. 13), Sanborn's (No. 33), Gravely's, Phelps's and Pierce's reports and the Confederate division reports remain deferred.

Rosecrans's, Pleasonton's and Curtis's reports, the subordinate Union and Confederate reports in Volume XLI Part 1, the organization of Price's army (No. 89), Maclean's itinerary (No. 90), the Price Court of Inquiry, Hinton's 1865 Rebel Invasion of Missouri and Kansas, maps and returns remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family (the NPS battle page plus the frozen Arnold rows). Wiley Britton's The Civil War on the Border, volume II (Putnam, 1899) is a retrospective history by a Union participant; by its preface the larger operations are based mainly on the published official reports, so it is not independent of the Price report family. Price's September 19 and November 2 dispatches and his December 28, 1864 report (Official Records Series I, Volume XLI, Part 1, No. 88) are one family of interested Confederate accounts. The Official Records volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
